The county treasurer is authorized to apply any unexpended balances of the one mill levy of 1908 for interest on railroad and past indebtedness bonds to the interest upon said bonds due July 1, 1909, and any portion thereof remaining unpaid shall be out of the one mill levy for interest upon said bonds under this Act. It appearing that bond No. 1, issue of 1881, in aid of G. & L. R. R., due January 1, 1908, has been cancelled, that the amount of that issue outstanding at the time the bonds were refunded by the issue of January 1, 1908, was five thousand dollars and not five thousand five hundred dollars, and that there is consequently a surplus from the proceeds of the issue of January 1, 1908, amounting to five hundred and twenty - one dollars and twenty - five cents, and also, that there is in the treasurer's hands a balance on account of refunding bonds of six hundred and seventy - five dollars and sixty - seven cents, the treasurer is authorized to apply this surplus to the issue of G. & L. R. R. bonds due January 1, 1909. The treasurer of Greenville county is authorized and directed to deposit in some reliable savings institution, at interest, payable on demand, five thousand five hundred dollars, proceeds of bond issue of thirty - five thousand dollars, July 1, 1907, to refund Air Line bonds of the issue of July 1, 1887, bonds to that amount being outstanding but not yet presented A. D. 1909. for payment. For payment to commissioners of sinking fund on account of loan of April 22, 1908, thirty - three thousand dollars; December 21, 1908, sixty - five hundred dollars, and.... 1909, sixty - four thousand dollars, one and one - half mills to be applied as follows: To loan of thirty - three thousand dollars, April 22, 1908, upon which it is estimated that there will be paid out of the levy of 1908 the sum of twelve thousand dollars, leaving a balance due of about twenty - two thousand dollars, there shall be paid sixty - five hundred dollars, the same being one - fifth (1-5) of the amount borrowed and the interest to January 1, 1910, estimated to be ten hundred and fifty dollars upon balance due after applying proceeds of levy of 1908; to loan of sixty - five hundred dollars, December 21, 1908, there shall be paid the sum of thirteen hundred dollars, the same being one - fifth (1-5) of the amount borrowed and the interest to January 1, 1910, three hundred thirty - four and 3-100 dollars; to the loan of sixty - four thousand dollars, authorized by Act of..... 1909, shall be paid the sum of sixty - four hundred dollars, the same being one - tenth (1-10) of the amount borrowed, and the interest to January 1, 1910, should less than said amount be available under this authorization, one - tenth of the amount borrowed shall be paid on January 1, 1910, together with interest due; and the remainder of the proceeds of the levy, if so much be necessary, shall be applied to the payment of interest due July 1, 1909, and January 1, 1910, upon bonds authorized by the Act of 1909. For payment of past indebtedness, one - half of one mill, to be applied to the following claims and any other valid past indebtedness and interest upon loans in anticipation of collection of taxes: On claim of National Bank of Greenville for claims paid on account of election upon the question of new courthouse, four hundred twenty - two and 90-100 dollars, and interest, twenty dollars; deficiency on account of Court expenses for 1908, nine hundred eighty - six and 51-100 dollars; for claims Nos. 3, 7, 17, 24, 25 and 26 allowed by the Supreme Court in the case of People's Bank against Goodwin, three hundred eighty - two and 20-100 dollars; deficiency on account of dispensary constables, five hundred four and 20-100 dollars; deficiency on account of post mortems andlunacy, two hundred ninety - seven and 57-100 dollars; deficiency on account of stationery and printing, one hundred eighty - eight and 30-100 dollars; deficiency on account of poorhouse and poor, two hundred sixty and 63-100 dollars; deficiency on account of public buildings, thirty - six and 50-100 dollars; balance due D. D. Davenport, one hundred twentyseven dollars, with interest at seven per cent. from December 30, 1908, to January 1, 1910, eight and 90-100 dollars; interest to January 1, 1909, on loans in anticipation of taxes, one hundred fourteen and 17-100 dollars; seventeen hundred three and 16-100 dollars; one hundred twenty - six and 33-100 dollars, and one hundred eighty - five and 17-100 dollars. Total past indebtedness, fifty - three hundred sixty - three and 53-100 dollars. All income from fines, fees, costs, commutation road tax, register of mesne conveyances office, and from all other sources, not otherwise appropriated by law, shall be paid to the county treasurer and be applicable to claims on account of ordinary county expenses, including convicts, roads and bridges for the current year. If any portion of any fund hereinbefore appropriated to the several items of ordinary county expenses remain unexpended, it shall be passed to a general contingent fund for the current year, to be used for any ordinary county purpose, other than convicts, roads and bridges, for which it may be needed. If there should be any surplus from the several funds hereinbefore appropriated, the county treasurer is directed to deposit the same in some reliable savings institution, at interest, for the purpose of accumulating a fund with which to put the county upon a cash basis. The supervisor shall not be authorized to draw any warrant upon the treasurer to be paid out of any of the several funds hereinbefore specifically appropriated, for any purpose other than that for which the same has been so appropriated, except as hereinbefore provided; and it shall be unlawful for the treasurer to pay any such inhibited warrant. It shall be unlawful for the county board of commissioners, or any member thereof, to create by contract, express or implied, any obligation against the county, which with the obligations then existing and payable out of any particular fund shall exceed the amount herein specifically appropriated therefor: Provided, That in case of emergency, with the written consent of the county delegation, this requirement may be dispensed with. Greenwood County - For ordinary county purposes, two (2) mills; for past indebtedness, one and one - half (1½) mills; for roads and bridges, three and one - half (3½) mills; for interest on railroad bonds, Ninety - Six township, two and three - fourths (234) mills; Cokesbury township, two (2) mills; Cooper township, three (3) mills, to be expended in the following manner: For county auditor, four hundred dollars; for county supervisor's, commissioners ' and clerk's salaries, fifteen hundred and fifty dollars; for county treasurer's salary, four hundred dollars; for county board of equalization, four hundred and seventy dollars; for jury, witness and constable tickets, three thousand five hundred dollars; for clerk of court, two hundred and fifty dollars; for sheriff, fourteen hundred dollars; for magistrates and constables, twenty - two hundred and fifty dollars; for coroner, one hundred dollars; for poor house and poor, fifteen hundred dollars; for repairs on roads and bridges, twenty - two thousand dollars; for repairs on public buildings, seven hundred dollars; for books, stationery and printing, nine hundred dollars; for contingent expenses, two thousand dollars; for post mortems, examining lunatics and conveying, seven hundred dollars; for jury commissioners and insurance, two hundred dollars; for interest on railroad bonds, four thousand two hundred dollars; for physician's and attorney's fees, two hundred dollars; for past indebtedness, nine thousand (9,000) dollars; for superintendent of education, eight hundred dollars: Provided, That out of the amount raised for ordinary county purposes, as above set forth, the county board of commisisoners. shall be authorized and empowered to pay a clerk to assist the auditor for a term of not more than two months, at a salary not to exceed the sum of forty (40) dollars per month. Hampton County - For ordinary county purposes, three (3) mills, for bridge and causeway across Coosawhatchie River Hampton. near Early Branch, as per Act of this General Assembly, threefourth (34) mill; for construction of a road from Hampton via Brunson to the Barnwell county line near Fairfax, and for the improvement of the roads in the county, two (2) mills. Horry County - For ordinary county purposes, three and one - half (32) mills; for roads and bridges, two (2) mills; courthouse and jail bonds, one (1) mill. Four (4) mills in Simpson Creek township, to pay the interest and part of principal on money borrowed to retire railroad bonds, issued to aid in the construction of the W. C. & C. Railroad, provided so much be necessary. Kershaw County - For the county of Kershaw, for ordinary county purposes, three and one - fourth (34) mills; for interest on railroad bonds, one and three - fourth (134) mills; for road tax, two (2) mills; for courthouse bonds, one - fourth of one (4) mill. Lancaster County - For ordinary county purposes, three and one - half (32) mills; for interest on Cheraw and Chester Railroad bonds, one (1) mill, and one - half of one (2) mill for sinking fund of said bonds; for roads and bridges, which fund shall be kept separate by the treasurer from the ordinary county fund, four (4) mills; for permanent bridges, one mill; for payment of interest on township bonds issued in aid of Charleston, Cincinnati and Chicago Railroad, the following special taxes are hereby imposed: In Pleasant Hill township, two and onehalf (22) mills; Gills Creek township, two and one - half (22) mills, and in Cane Creek township, two and one - half (2½) mills: Provided, That the county treasurer shall apply to the payment of interest on bonds of said township the funds arising from the property of the South Carolina and Georgia Extension Railroad Company in Lancaster county on the levy for ordinary county purposes, to be applied to said interests in proportion to the amount of the bonds of said township, respectively, outstanding. The county commissioners are hereby directed to use all funds in the county treasury or in the banks, belonging to Pleasant Hill township, to purchase and retire the bonds of said township, or to invest said funds in any other like bonds. The treasurer is hereby required to keep all funds now in his hands, or hereafter collected by him, for the retirement of township or county bonds on deposit with the banks of Lancaster county at interest. Said funds and all other funds belonging to the county shall be kept on deposit with said banks, said deposits to be in proportion to the taxes paid by the said banks, respectively. The fees of witnesses in the Court of General A. D. 1909. Sessions shall be fifty cents per day and mileage as now provided by law. It shall be unlawful for the county commissioners to support any pauper, wholly or in part, except in the county poorhouse. Laurens County - For the county of Laurens, for ordinary county purposes, three and one - fourth (34) mills; for roads. and bridges, three (3) mills; for interest on railroad bonds, one (1) mill. The dispensary fund going to the county shall be applied to the past school indebtedness of this county. The county supervisor is hereby authorized to borrow money, not exceeding in amount the three mills school tax, and to pledge the ordinary three mills school tax for the payment of said loan or loans in order to run the public school of the county for the present year on a cash basis. The county supervisor is hereby authorized to draw his warrant for, and the county treasurer pay, the judge of probate of said county the sum of one hundred dollars out of the ordinary county funds for the present year for the stationery, stamps and other incidental expenses of the said office. Lee County - For the county of Lee, for ordinary county purposes, four (4) mills; for sinking fund, one and three - fourths (134) mills. The county supervisor is hereby authorized to draw his warrant, and the county treasurer to pay same in favor of J. D. Galloway to satisfy a certain judgment obtained against said county for $ 200, and costs. The county treasurer is hereby authorized to honor the warrant of the supervisor in favor of the courthouse commission for $ 900, the same being proceeds of a lot sold belonging to the county of Lee, and in the further sum of not exceeding $ 1,000, both of said sums to be expended in the improving of the courthouse square. Lexington County - For the county of Lexington, for ordinary county purposes, three and one - half mills (3 %); for inLexington. terest on C., N. & L. bonds, Saluda, Broad River and Fork townships, seven and one - half mills (7 %); special levy for permanent road building, one and one - fourth mills (14). For W. Q. Jackson, account of proposed Edisto county, forty - six and 50-100 dollars; for Paul E. Hutto, commissioner, account proposed Edisto county, eighteen and 60-100 dollars; for the Brookland Light Infantry, at New Brookland, one hundred dollars; and the county commissioners are authorized and directed to issue their pay certificates for, and the treasurer to pay, such Marion amounts. Marion County - For salaries, two (2) mills, as follows: Sheriff, eighteen hundred dollars, and two hundred dollars for service of magistrates ' papers; supervisor, one thousand dollars; superintendent of education, eight hundred dollars; county commissioners, four hundred dollars; clerk for county commissioners, four hundred dollars; clerk of court, five hundred dollars; county treasurer, four hundred dollars; auditor, three hundred and twelve dollars; magistrates and constables, three thousand dollars; coroner, one hundred and seventy - five dollars; witnesses, jurors and court constables, three thousand dollars; dieting jail prisoners, seven hundred dollars; post mortem examinations, lunatics, five hundred dollars; county board of equalization, three hundred and fifty dollars; which amounts shall be paid quarterly except those items the public good demands otherwise. For roads and bridges, one and three - fourths of one (134) mills; for poorhouse and poor, one and one - fourth (14) mills, as follows: For poorhouse and poor, forty - five hundred dollars; for contingent fund, five thousand dollars; stationery and printing, five hundred dollars; county board of education, fifty dollars: Provided, That there shall be kept a ledger account with each item herein appropriated, and that in all contracts and accounts for the expenditure of all moneys not salaries, the county commissioners shall have equal authority with county supervisor, and no account shall be paid for merchandise, material or other purpose, unless at least one of the board shall have personal knowledge of the work done, material furnished or completion of contract, before paying such claim: And provided, further, That all contracts for public printing shall be paid for at the legal rate and divided equally among The Marion Star, The Mullins Enterprise, and The Dillon Herald: And provided, further, That the various funds arising from the levies herein made, shall be applied only to the purposes herein named, and that five mills shall cover all levies made for Marion county for 1909: And provided, further, That the contingent fund arising from the levies, as hereinbefore OF SOUTH CAROLINA. 257 stated, shall be applied as follows: Seventy - five (75) per cent. A. D. 1909. of said funds for water, lights, fuel and insurance for courthouse, clerk's office and jail physician's salary, attorney's fees, janitor for courthouse and clerk's office, reindexing records in clerk of court's office as hereinafter provided, blankets and heating for jail, repairs on public buildings, and the other twenty - five (25) per cent. of said fund shall be applied to such incidental expenses as may arise: And provided, further, That all balances from any fund of 1908 or previous years, be brought forward to the general fund for 1909, and the county commissioners and county treasurer are authorized, from time to time, to borrow such amounts of money as may be required, and to pledge the taxes herein levied, not to exceed threefourths of the taxes so levied, and a first lien shall be given to parties loaning the money herein provided for: Provided, further, That the county commissioners of said county are hereby authorized to draw their warrants on the county treasurer for the sum of one thousand dollars in favor of J. Clement Davis, S. M. Davis, J. D. Montgomery and S. G. Miles, committee, who are hereby authorized to use the same in the purchase and distribution of planting seed for the crop of 1909 among the flood sufferers in said county, who, in the judgment of said committee, are deserving and needing such assistance. Marlboro County - For ordinary county purposes, six mills: Provided, That the county supervisor shall have authority to Marlboro. borrow for the use of the county a sum not exceeding fifteen thousand dollars, and that said supervisor shall have authority to pay any rate of interest on such loans not exceeding six per cent. per annum for the year A. D. 1909. Newberry County - For the county of Newberry, for ordinary county purposes, three and one - half (32) mills, one - half Newberry. (%) of one mill to pay on past indebtedness, and to be used exclusively for such purpose. The county supervisor is hereby authorized and empowered to borrow from the sinking fund commission, for current expenses, a sum not exceeding twenty thousand dollars, at a rate of interest not greater than five per cent. per annum, but in the event the said amount cannot be obtained from the said sinking fund commission, then the said county supervisor is hereby authorized and empowered to bor-row from any other source an amount not exceeding twenty thousand dollars, at a rate of interest not exceeding six per cent. per annum. For the payment of said loan, the ordinary county taxes for the year 1909 shall be pledged upon the note or notes of the county supervisor and county treasurer. Oconee County - For the county of Oconee, for ordinary county purposes, three (3) mills; for roads, bridges and ferries, two (2) mills; for interest on the county bonds, one - half of one mil !; for sinking fund for the purpose of retiring county bonds, one - fourth (4) mill. The county board of commissioners are authorized to borrow from the sinking fund commission or other source the sum of fifteen thonsand dollars for the payment of back indebtedness and current expenses and pledge the tax levy for the payment thereof, and the sinking fund is authorized to make said loan. Orangeburg County - For ordinary county purposes and back Orangeburg. indebtedness, two and one - half (22) mills. Pickens County - For ordinary county purposes, five (5) mills; past indebtedness, one - half of one mill; for chaingang, two mills; for dispensary constables, one - half of one mill. Richland County - For the county of Richdand, for ordinary county purposes, two and one - half mills, and an additional tax of two mills in the school district of the city of Columbia, in lieu of any special tax authorized to be levied by an Act entitled " An Act to provide for the establishment of a new school district in Richland county, and to authorize the levy and collection of the local tax therein, " approved December 24, 1880; an additional tax of two mills in school district No. 12, in lieu of the special tax authorized by an election in said district under and in accordance with Section 1208 of Volume I of the Code of 1902, as amended. The proceeds of the said two and one - half mills tax, together with the other funds available for use by the board of county commissioners, shall be expended as follows, to wit: for erection of cotton platform in the city of Columbia, as provided for in an Act of 1909, two thousand dollars, if so much be necessary; for maintenance of county police system, as provided for in an Act of 1909, three thousand and seven hundred dollars, if so much be necessary; for expert examination of records and A. D. 1909. amounts of receipts and disbursements and other acts of the county officers of Richland county for the past four years and for the year 1909, one thousand dollars, if so much be necessary, said examination to be made under the supervision of the grand jury, by a chartered auditing company, or a member of the Association of Chartered Accountants selected or approved by the presiding judge; for roads, bridges and chaingang, thirty - five thousand dollars, if so much be necessary: Provided, however, That all contracts for supplies of whatever kind, including all purchases for poorhouse, chaingang and every other purpose, shall be upon competitive bids every three months after advertisements for at least two weeks previous thereto in four issues of one of the daily papers published in the city of Columbia, and contracts shall be awarded to the lowest responsible bidder for the period of three months; award for supplies as hereinbefore provided for shall be based on delivery of said supplies at the county courthouse: Provided, further, That no bills or accounts against the county shall be paid after the first day of April, A. D. 1909, unless previously contracted for by such competition and unless the claim be filed for audit within thirty days from the furnishing of the supplies or whatever the said claim may be for: Provided, further, That each magistrate in said county shall attend on Monday and Friday of each week from 10 to 12 o'clock in the forenoon at the precinct at which he was elected and keep his office open on said days for said hours for the convenience of the people having business in his court, and shall make and file with the clerk of the Court of General Sessions of said county each month a report of all criminal cases begun before him and of their status or disposition, and of all fines collected: Provided, further, That the constable of each magistrate in said county shall make and file with the clerk of the Court of General Sessions a report covering name of each and every criminal proceeding in which a warrant or other process has been issued to him, with the name of the magistrate issuing the same, the date of the process and the disposition thereof by said constable; and the said board of county commissioners shall not pay any salaries of magistrates or constables any month until said reports have been made and filed as herein required; and the accountants employed to examine, audit and report on the books of the supervisor and the treasurer in said county shall annually examine the reports submitted by the said constables and compare the same with the reports and the dockets of the magistrates, which shall be furnished to them for the purpose, and make report thereof to the board of county commissioners and to the foreman of the grand jury, showing any irregularities or discrepancies therein. Saluda County - For the county of Saluda, for ordinary county purposes; six and one - half mills. Past indebtedness one - half mill. The county board of commissioners of said county are hereby authorized and empowered to borrow a sum sufficient for the purpose of defraying expenses of the county for the fiscal year 1909 and to pay past indebtedness in such amounts and at such times as to them may seem proper: Provided, That the sum so borrowed shall not exceed the sum of seventeen thousand dollars, at not exceeding seven per cent. interest. The levy herein made may be pledged as security for the payment of the loans so made. Spartanburg County - For the county of Spartanburg, for ordinary county purposes, three and one - half mills; for ordinary road purposes, one mill; for interest on bonds, one mill; sinking fund, one mill; permanent improvement on highways, one - half of one mill; for bridges, one - half of one mill. The accounts for each of those funds shall be kept separately by the county treasurer and the board of county commissioners, and any use or application of any of said funds for any other purpose than as above named shall be a breach of trust. In anticipation of the collection of taxes, as hereinbefore levied for the said several purposes, the county supervisor and county treasurer are hereby authorized to borrow not exceeding eighty - five per cent. of the amount levied for any one purpose as shown by the auditor's duplicate, and to pledge the levy for such purpose to secure such loan. Any obligation given for an amount above said eighty - five per cent. shall be null and void. No greater interest than seven per cent. per annum shall be paid for any such borrowed money. The county authorities are hereby forbidden to expend a greater amount than sixty per cent. of the levy for ordinary county purposes prior to the first day of July, The time for the payment of road taxes for Spartanburg A. D. 1909. county shall not expire until March the sixteenth, 1909. Sumter County - For the county of Sumter, for ordinary Sumter. county purposes, two and three - fourths mills; special levy to pay loan to sinking fund commission, under the Act of 1907, one (1) mill. That the county commissioners be authorized to borrow a sum not exceeding three thousand ($ 3,000) dollars, to be expended in defraying expenses of maintaining and building roads and bridges, and for these purposes only: Provided, That the rate of interest or discount shall not exceed seven per centum per annum: Provided, further, That the county commissioners be allowed to use for the same purposes and to purchase road machinery and implements the net surplus accruing to the county from the dispensary profits, after the payment of the ordinary county expenses: And provided, That the other and ordinary functions of the county be not impaired or interfered with. That the county commissioners be authorized and directed to pay over to the Sumter County Association for the Suppression of Tuberculosis (or the association working under this or some similar name) the sum of five hundred dollars, to be used in said county for the suppression of said dread disease in said county, and shall require from the association to whom said sum is paid complete vouchers showing how said sum was expended. That the county commissioners shall go over and inspect the roads and bridges of said county and make a report to the county board of commissioners of such inspection, and condition of said roads and bridges, each commissioner to inspect and report upon the condition of the roads and bridges in the section of the county in which he resides, as near as practicable; that such inspection shall be made quarterly, and for such inspection and report made by such commissioners they shall each receive the sum of five dollars, but no mileage. For rent of armory and fixtures for the Sumter Light Infantry, one hundred and fifty ($ 150) dollars. That the sum of twenty - two and 50-100 dollars be, and is hereby, ordered to be paid to the sheriff of Sumter county for the advertising of certain land for sale for taxes. That the county board of commissioners of said county be authorized and directed to furnish and supply to the several magistrates of said county official blanks and supplies, including dockets. That the fund or money raised or collected under the Act of 1908 to purchase road machinery, etc., be covered into the ordinary county fund. That the county board of commissioners be authorized to use and expend for the purpose of building and maintaining roads and bridges in said county all funds and money raised hereunder not otherwise directed to be expended or used, that is to say, that any surplus may be so used for said purposes. Union County - For ordinary county purposes, three and three - fourths mills; interest railroad bonds, one mill; old veterans, one - fourth mill; past indebtedness, State sinking fund, one mill; past indebtedness, general, and for bridges, roads, three and one - half mills; roads, one mill. Williamsburg County - For ordinary county purposes, two Williamsburg and three - fourths mills; that the sheriff shall be paid two hundred and fifty dollars; the clerk of court, one hundred and twenty - five dollars; J. N. Hammett, county commissioner, three hundred dollars; Cable Piano Co., twenty - five dollars; J. M. Eaddy, thirty - three dollars and thirty - three cents. The county commissioners are authorized and directed to issue their pay certificates for and the treasurer to pay such amounts in addition to the salaries of said officers, now provided by law: Provided, That the commutation road tax for 1909 shall be two dollars, in lieu of four days ' work, instead of one dollar or four days, as heretofore provided by law. York County - For the county of York, for ordinary county purposes, four (4) mills; a levy of two (2) mills for road purposes, as provided by law, the treasurer to apportion same, as required by law; also a special levy of one - half (½) mill, for the purpose of the erection of a bridge over Broad River, as provided in the Act in regard thereto; in Ebenezer township, a special levy of three - fourths (34) of one mill; in Catawba township, a special levy of one and three - fourths (134) mills; in York township, a special levy of two and one - half (2½) mills, to pay the interest on bonds issued by said townships in interest of the Charleston, Cincinnati and Chicago Railroad; also in said townships of Ebenezer, Catawba and York a special levy of one - half (½) mill, as a sinking fund, to retire said bonds; the treasurer of York county for collecting and distri- buting this special levy shall be allowed commissions, as now A. D. 1909. provided by law. The county commissioners of York county are hereby authorized and empowered to borrow a sum of money, not exceeding fourteen thousand dollars, at rate of interest not to exceed six per cent., for ordinary county purposes, and to pledge the tax levy of said county to secure the same: Provided, That $ 4,000 thereof shall be used, if so much be necessary, in furnishing the county jail with iron or steel cells, one - half of which may be paid 1910. In addition to this amount for ordinary county purposes, the county commissioners of York county are authorized and empowered to borrow a sum of not exceeding five thousand dollars, at rate of interest not to exceed six per cent., for the purpose of erecting a bridge, along with Cherokee county, over Broad River, and to pledge the special tax levy of one - half (½) mill to reduce the same.

The township boards of education in this state, in their respective townships, and the several other boards of education, and the trustees, visitors and directors of schools, or other officers having authority in the premises, of each city or incorporated village, shall be and they are hereby authorized and required to establish, within their respective jurisdictions, one or more separate schools for colored children, when the whole number, by enumeration, exceeds twenty, and when such schools will afford them, as far as practicable, the advantages and privileges of a common school education and all such schools so established for colored children, shall be under the control and management of the board of education, or other school officers who have in charge the educational interests of the other schools and such schools for colored children shall be continued in operation each year until the full share of all the school funds of the township or district belonging to said colored children, on the basis of enumeration, shall have been expended provided, that when the number of colored children residing in adjoining townships or districts, whether in the same or in different counties, shall exceed twenty, the boards of education of said townships or districts so situated, may form a joint district for the education of colored children, and said school shall be under the control and direction of the board of education of the township or district in which the school-house is situated. When the whole number of colored children enumerated is less than twenty, or when owing to the great distance they reside from each other a separate school for colored children is impracticable, the board of education shall set apart the full share of school funds raised on the number of said colored children, and the money so set apart shall be appropriated each year for the education of such colored children, under the direction of the board.
b_text: Section 1. Appropriation for Teaching of Agriculture.—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State: To promote the teaching of agriculture in the public schools, there is hereby annually appropriated out of the State Treasury five thousand dollars ($5,000.00), to be expended as hereinafter provided by the State Superintendent of Education, in consolidated schools doing practical class room and field work in agriculture. § 2. How Districts May Receive Benefits of Act—Teacher— Duties —Whenever the Boards of Trustees of three or more school districts shall raise from regular funds, local taxes, private subscriptions, or otherwise, and shall deposit with the County Treasurer not less than $750.00 to be expended by the County Board of Education upon their warrant, duly approved by the County Superintendent, for the teaching of agriculture in their respective districts,.such group of districts shall be entitled to $750.00 from the State. All funds raised by the respective Boards of Trustees, or supplied by the State, shall be used to pay the salary of a trained teacher of agriculture, who shall do classroom instruction field work on the school farm, school garden or school orchard, or in any other line of agricultural teaching needed in the territory composing the districts. Such trained agricultural teacher may serve as Superintendent or Principal of the group of co-operating schools, shall reside during the twelve months of the year in the territory he serves, shall possess all the scholarship requirements regularly demanded of other teachers, shall hold a valid certificate duly registered in the County Superintendent’s office and shall be subject to the same supervision as other teachers in State aided schools. He shall make all reports required of public school teachers, and, in addition thereto, shall furnish such other special reports as may be required in his special field. § 3. Term of Teacher’s Service.—Any such teacher of agriculture shall be employed jointly by the co-operating Boards of Trustees, the County Board of Education and the State Superintendent of Education. But any contract for the employment of such teacher shall require at least three years consecutive service and each such contract of employment shall be signed by the legal repre- sentatives of the district, the County Superintendent’s office, and the State Superintendent’s office. § 4. Requirements for Schools Under This Act.—Any public school co-operating in this work shall have an enrollment of at least seventy-five pupils with a regular attendance of at least forty pupils, three teachers of the usual public school subjects, a term of seven months, a local tax of eight mills, a comfortable and sanitary building of at least three rooms, a school site of not less than two acres, the minimum equipment prescribed by the State Board of Education and shall use the téxt books and course of study regularly required of other public schools. The special lessons or course in Agriculture may be adapted to the community needs as recognized by the Agricultural teacher, and such teacher shall have full right and absolute freedom in the introduction and presentation of any additional lessons, bulletins, instructions, or other matter that may be furnished by the United States Department of Agriculture, the State Department of Agriculture, Clemson College or any other agricultural college or experiment station. All such modifications of the course of study shall be reported in writing to the County Superintendent of Education and to the State Superintendent of Education, and shall not be continued in any school over the disapproval of the State Board of Education. § 5. Enrollment of Pupils—Any school receiving State aid for agricultural teaching shall enroll free of charge any pupil, fourteen years of age or upward, desiring to pursue such a course and possessing sufficient knowledge of the elementary public school subjects to enable him, in the opinion of the agricultural teacher, to do this work with advantage. Schools receiving aid for agricultural work shall not be ineligible to share in the State appropriations for term extension, rural graded schools or high schools. § 6. Certain Aid May Be Sought.—In the furtherance of this work, District, County and State school officers may invite the co-operation, advice and inspection of Clemson College, the Farm Demonstration forces, the State Department of Agriculture, or the United States Department of Agriculture, and the basis for this co-operation shall be determined by all the agencies interested. § 7. Text Book—The State Board of Education is hereby authorized to adopt a textbook on agriculture to be taught in all other schools not provided for in this Act. § 8. Inconsistent Acts Repealed.—All Acts or parts of Acts inconsistent with this Act are hereby repealed.
